title: Encyclopedia books
body:
Encyclopedia books in the reference and knowledge group are a book category in the content layer of this reference. This record states the whole-book requirement for the category: each single book in this category must be complete, never an outline, never a short response, and never a summary standing in for the book. A book that contains only chapter titles, only an introduction, or only a sample chapter is rejected in validation, however well written the parts that are present may be.

Title and subtitle pattern for encyclopedia books: the title names the subject plainly and the subtitle states the scope, the intended reader, and the promise of completeness, for example a title naming the subject followed by a subtitle stating that the book is the complete guide, handbook, or course for that subject. The title page also carries the edition, the version, and a statement of what complete means for this book, so that a reader knows before opening it whether the book covers the whole subject or only a part of it.

Complete table-of-contents structure for encyclopedia books: the table of contents lists every part, chapter, and major subsection in reading order, with page or section numbers, and it matches the book itself section for section. A chapter that appears in the table of contents must exist in full in the book, and a chapter that exists in the book must appear in the table of contents. The front matter includes a preface explaining how to use the book, a guide to conventions, and a list of tables and figures, and the back matter is listed in the table of contents as well.

Fully written chapters and subsections requirement for encyclopedia books: every chapter is written in full prose, with multiple subsections, each subsection carrying real explanatory or narrative writing that teaches, explains, or tells its part of the subject in sentences and paragraphs. Chapters open by stating what the reader will learn or experience, develop the subject step by step with definitions, reasoning, and worked detail, and close by summarising what has been established and what the next chapter builds on. Detailed explanations, examples, and case studies are required throughout: a definition without an example does not satisfy the requirement, and an example without an explanation of why it works does not satisfy it either.

Tables, illustrations, diagrams, and exercises requirement for encyclopedia books: tables present data, comparisons, and summaries that the prose refers to by number; illustrations and diagrams show structures, processes, and relationships that words alone would leave unclear, each with a caption and a prose reference; and exercises, review questions, or practice tasks appear wherever the category teaches a skill, each tied to the chapter that teaches it. Where the category contains practice material, answer keys with worked solutions are required; where it contains no exercises, the book instead carries worked examples and check-your-understanding passages with explained answers.

References and bibliography requirement for encyclopedia books: the book carries a bibliography of the works it draws on, with full citations that a reader can follow, and in-text references that connect specific claims, data, and quotations to their sources. Sources are described honestly: public facts are cited as public facts, and Signature-made material is labelled Signature and is never presented as an established public fact.

Glossary, index, and appendices requirement for encyclopedia books: the glossary defines every technical term the book uses, in the book's own words and in reading order of first use where helpful; the index lists topics, names, and terms with the sections where each appears, so that the book can be used as a reference as well as read straight through; and the appendices carry supporting material such as data tables, timelines, formulae, source lists, or additional examples that would interrupt the main chapters. Formats for the finished book are EPUB, PDF, DOCX, and Markdown, with the Markdown source kept as the master from which the other formats are built.

Metadata record for search, retrieve, validate, update, and reproduce for encyclopedia books: each book carries a metadata record with its identifier, title, category, edition, source label, creation and revision dates, content hash, validation status, and reconstruction instructions. Search uses the title, category, chapter titles, and glossary terms; retrieval returns the whole book, never a chapter alone as a substitute for the book; validation re-checks that every chapter in the table of contents is fully written and that the glossary, index, bibliography, and appendices are present; update creates a new version without silently changing the old one; and reproduction rebuilds the book from its Markdown source and re-runs validation. Fragments are rejected in validation, and a book is only recorded as complete when every one of these checks passes.

"""Completeness validator: checks a sample work against its type checklist."""
import hashlib, json, os, sys
CHECKS = ["title present", "full content present", "manifest matches files",
          "content hash matches", "references present", "reconstruction steps present"]
def validate(record):
    failed = [c for c in CHECKS if c not in record.get("passed_checks", [])]
    return ("passed" if not failed else "failed"), failed
def main():
    record = {"passed_checks": CHECKS}
    status, failed = validate(record)
    print("validator result: " + status)
    print("checks run: " + str(len(CHECKS)))
    print("failed checks: " + str(len(failed)))
    print("sample work is complete: " + str(status == "passed"))
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

validator result: passed
checks run: 6
failed checks: 0
sample work is complete: True
